  • Trainer greeting texts

docs.title: Transports
docs.text: Boats and zeppelins between continents are moving game objects (src/game/Transports/TransportMgr.cpp). Their routes come from client data; SQL only tweaks timing.

docs.title: How a Transport Is Assembled
docs.text:
1. Template - gameobject_template entry with type = 15 (MO_TRANSPORT - boats/zeppelins). Its data0 holds the taxi path id.
  2. Route - TransportMgr::GenerateWaypoints reads that path from client TaxiPathNode.dbc (sTaxiPathNodesByPath) and builds a smoothed spline with map-change teleport points between continents.
  3. Timing - stop frames, acceleration and cruise segments are computed automatically from path geometry.
  4. Override - transports may correct the result: a non-zero period replaces the computed round-trip duration. Rows are selected per client build.

docs.title: Passengers
docs.text:
• Players and NPCs board by walking onto the object; their movement updates stream relative to the transport while attached (GenericTransport::AddFollower…).
  • Disembarking happens automatically at stop frames or on logout.
  • Being on a transport affects spell/LOs handling - transports count as the passenger's map position anchor.

docs.title: Adding / Fixing a Route
docs.text:
You cannot draw new routes in SQL: they require a taxi path in the client data. In SQL you can:

  • point a custom GO template of type 15 (MO_TRANSPORT) at an existing taxi path id,
  • adjust the cycle time via transports.period,
  • gate variants per client build (build column).

docs.title: Troubleshooting Startup DB Errors
docs.text: The world server validates the database at startup and prints LOG_DBERROR messages for bad rows. This page maps the most common messages to causes and fixes.

docs.title: Loot
docs.text:
Message Meaning Fix Table 'X' entry %d item %d: maxcount value (%u) to large... maxcount > 255 lower maxcount ...has condition_id %u that does not exist in 'conditions', ignoring dangling condition reference create the condition or set 0 mincountOrRef %i < 0 and has condition ... requires a player and is not supported reference rows can't use player-dependent conditions move condition to child rows / drop it Table '%s' loot id #%u used but it doesn't have records. a creature/GO/item references an empty loot table add rows to that entry >> Loaded 0 loot definitions. DB table '%s' is empty. store empty; benign for optional stores like junk/fail pools fill if referenced

Unused-loot warnings (ReportUnusedIds) list entries nobody references: delete them or wire them up.

docs.title: Creatures & Templates
docs.text: Message Fix Creature (GUID: %u) does not exist but has a record in 'creature_addon' remove orphan addon row Creature (Entry: %u) is using display_id%d (%u), but creature_display_info_addon data is missing add addon row for the display or change display id Creature id %u listed in 'creature_charm_spells' does not exist. fix entry Creature id %u listed in 'petcreateinfo_spell' not exist. fix entry

docs.title: Broadcast Text & Sounds
docs.text: Message Fix BroadcastText (Id: %u) ... has ChatType %u but this chat type does not exist. fix ChatType (say/yell/emote…) BroadcastText (Id: %u) ... has EmoteId2/3 ... invalid emote ids → correct or zero them BroadcastText (Id: %u) ... SoundId %u but sound does not exist. point at sound_entries id or clear BroadcastText (Id: %u) in table 'locales_broadcast_text' does not exist. Skipped! locale row without base row - delete it Entry %i in table '%s' has Emote %u but emote does not exist. quest/greeting emote ids

docs.title: Quests, Skills, Fishing
docs.text: Message Fix AreaId %u defined in 'skill_fishing_base_level' does not exist wrong area id quest referenced by *_questrelation doesn't exist add the quest or remove the relation

docs.title: General Workflow
docs.text:
1. Reproduce: restart mangosd and capture full log (grep LOG_DBERROR).
  2. Fix data, not code: these errors are almost always data bugs.
  3. Reload where possible: many stores support .reload <store> commands (GM Commands); otherwise restart.
  4. Re-check with a fresh log until clean.

A clean startup log is the baseline for content work: new errors then stand out immediately.

docs.title: Tutorial: Adding a Custom NPC
docs.text: End-to-end example: a talkative guard NPC for Stormwind that greets players, responds when greeted with /bow, and drops a custom item. Everything is database-only.

docs.title: 1. Template
docs.text:
INSERT INTO creature_template
(entry, name, subname, display_id1, level_min, level_max, faction, npc_flags,
 gossip_menu_id, ai_name, movement_type, rank, script_name)
VALUES
(90001, 'Stormwind Town Crier', 'Herald of Goldshire', 4975, 60, 60, 12,
 1, 90001, 'EventAI', 0, 0, '');
  • faction = 12 - stormwind-friendly.
  • npc_flags = 1 - gossip enabled.
  • ai_name = 'EventAI' - table-driven AI (see AI System).

Check the exact column names in creature_template - the table carries many more (stats, resistances…), defaults are fine for a friendly NPC.

docs.title: 2. Spawn
docs.text:
INSERT INTO creature (guid, id, map, position_x, position_y, position_z, orientation,
                      spawntimesecsmin, spawntimesecsmax, movement_type)
VALUES (5000000, 90001, 0, -9464.13, 61.94, 56.34, 2.42, 300, 300, 0);

Pick an unused guid; map 0 = Eastern Kingdoms. Movement types are explained in the Movement System.

docs.title: 3. Greeting Text
docs.text:
-- menu id 90001 shows text 90001
INSERT INTO broadcast_text (entry, male_text) VALUES (90001, 'Hail, traveler! Need directions?');
INSERT INTO npc_text (ID, BroadcastTextID0) VALUES (90001, 90001);
INSERT INTO gossip_menu (entry, text_id) VALUES (90001, 90001);

Flow details: Gossip System.

docs.title: 4. Bow Response (EventAI)
docs.text:
-- event: on receive emote → action scripts 900010 and 900011
INSERT INTO creature_ai_events (id, creature_id, event_type, event_chance, event_param1,
                                action1_script, action2_script, comment)
VALUES (9000101, 90001, 22 /*RECEIVE_EMOTE*/, 100, 17 /*TEXTEMOTE_BOW = /bow*/,
        900010, 900011, 'Crier bows back');

INSERT INTO creature_ai_scripts (id, command, datalong, dataint, comments)
VALUES (900010, 0 /*TALK*/, 1 /*CHAT_TYPE_YELL*/, 90002, 'Crier yells a greeting'),
       (900011, 1 /*EMOTE*/, 2 /*EMOTE_ONESHOT_BOW*/, 1, 'bow emote');

The TALK command reads texts from broadcast_text - add entry 90002 there. Full command reference: DB Script Tables.

docs.title: 5. Optional Loot
docs.text:
UPDATE creature_template SET loot_id = 90001 WHERE entry = 90001;
INSERT INTO creature_loot_template (entry, item, ChanceOrQuestChance)
VALUES (90001, 900001, 25);   -- 25% drop of item 900001

Loot mechanics: Loot System.

docs.title: 6. Localization (optional)
docs.text: Add rows to locales_creature and locales_broadcast_text with _locN columns filled (see Localization).

docs.title: 7. Verify
docs.text:
.npc info 90001          -- template loaded?
.go creature 5000000     -- teleport to spawn
.reload creature_template -- after template edits

Watch the server log for LOG_DBERROR lines mentioning your entries.

docs.title: Tutorial: Adding a Custom Quest
docs.text: A kill-and-collect quest for the NPC from Adding a Custom NPC: bring 5 Crier Tokens (item 900001) and earn gold + an item reward.

docs.title: 1. Quest Template
docs.text:
INSERT INTO quest_template
(entry, Method, MinLevel, QuestLevel, RequiredRaces, Title, Details,
 Objectives, EndText, ReqItemCount1, ReqItemId1, RewOrReqMoney, RewXP,
 RewItemId1, RewItemCount1)
VALUES
(90002, 2, 10, 15, 1 /*human only*/, 'Tokens of Gratitude',
 'The crier asked me to gather his tokens back from the ruffians in Elwynn.',
 'Bring 5 Crier Tokens to the Stormwind Town Crier.', 'You found them all!',
 5, 900001, 1500, 3, 900002, 1);

Key groups explained: Quest System. Column list: quest_template.

docs.title: 2. Give & Take
docs.text:
-- offered by our NPC (creature_questrelation = giver)
INSERT INTO creature_questrelation (id, quest) VALUES (90001, 90002);

-- turned in to the same NPC
INSERT INTO creature_involvedrelation (id, quest) VALUES (90001, 90002);

docs.title: 3. The Objective Item
docs.text:
INSERT INTO item_template (entry, class, name, display_id, Quality, Flags,
                           Bonding, BuyPrice, SellPrice, InventoryType, stackable)
VALUES (900001, 12 /*quest item*/, 'Crier Token', 6440, 1, 32768, 1, 25, 6, 0, 5);

Quest items use class 12; adding flag 0x8000 (NO_DISENCHANT) prevents players disenchanting them; class 12 alone is what makes them quest items.

docs.title: 4. Reward Item (optional)
docs.text: Insert item 900002 similarly with a real quality/class - or reuse any existing entry.

docs.title: 5. Chain It (optional)
docs.text:
UPDATE quest_template SET NextQuestId = 90003 WHERE entry = 90002;

Flow-control fields (PrevQuestId, ExclusiveGroup, NextQuestInChain…) are documented in the Quest System overview.

docs.title: 6. Localization (optional)
docs.text: Fill Title_locN, Details_locN, … in locales_quest - see Localization.

docs.title: 7. Verify
docs.text:
.reload quest_template
.quest add 90002      -- self-test as GM
.additem 900001 5     -- simulate objective progress

Common load errors logged at startup: missing ReqItemId, wrong race/class masks, or a quest attached to a creature that does not exist.

docs.title: World Database Tables
docs.text: The world database is mostly static and contains definitions for all game content like items, creatures and quests. Each table is documented below.

docs.title: Tables
docs.text:
• DB-Script-Tables - The generic script command set shared by all the script tables.
  • area_template - Contains information about all areas and zones of the world, including flags, recommended level, faction ownership, and liquid type.
  • areatrigger_bg_entrance - Defines battleground entrance portals that players can use to join the queue.
  • areatrigger_involvedrelation - Associates area triggers with quest completion.
  • areatrigger_scripts - Scripts executed when a player enters an area trigger.
  • areatrigger_tavern - Defines area triggers that act as inns/taverns.
  • areatrigger_teleport - Defines where area triggers (like dungeon portals) teleport players, and the conditions required to use them.
  • areatrigger_template - Defines the location, size, and shape of all area triggers.
  • auctionhousebot - Defines items that will be sold by the Auction House Bot (simulated economy).
  • autobroadcast - Defines messages sent periodically to all online players.
  • battleground_events - Defines events that spawn creatures and gameobjects during battleground matches.
  • battleground_template - Defines core parameters for each battleground: team sizes, level range, spawn locations, and reward spells.
  • battlemaster_entry - Defines which creatures are battlemasters and which battleground they represent.
  • broadcast_text - Central repository for in-game NPC text strings.
  • cinematic_waypoints - Defines camera positions at specific times during intro cinematics.
  • command - Overrides the default security level and provides help text for in-game chat commands.
  • conditions - Provides a flexible conditional logic system used by scripts, gossip, quests, teleports, etc.
  • creature - Contains creature spawn data (placement, respawn, movement, and overrides).
  • creature_addon - Provides per-spawn overrides for creature visual state, equipment, mount, emotes, and auras.
  • creature_ai_events - Defines events that trigger scripts for creatures using EventAI.
  • creature_ai_scripts - Actions executed by EventAI events.
  • creature_battleground - Links creature spawns to battleground events, allowing specific NPCs to react to battleground state changes.
  • creature_charm_spells - Defines spells available on the pet bar of charmed creatures (e.g., mind-controlled mobs).
  • creature_classlevelstats - Base stats for creatures by class and level - health, mana, damage, armor, and primary attributes.
  • creature_display_info_addon - Additional data for creature display info - bounding radius, combat reach, movement speeds, and gender.
  • creature_equip_template - Defines held items by creatures (main hand, off hand, ranged).
  • creature_groups - Groups creatures into formations, with a leader and relative positions.
  • creature_groups_entry_limit - Restricts the number of creatures of a specific creature id that can be part of a group.
  • creature_involvedrelation - Maps creatures (NPCs) to quests that they end, the turn-in side of the relation pair (offer side: creature_questrelation).
  • creature_linking - Links creatures so they aggro / evade / respawn together.
  • creature_linking_template - Template-level creature linking - all spawns of a given entry link to a master entry on a specific map.
  • creature_loot_template - Loot tables for creatures - defines items, drop chances, groups, and patch ranges.
  • creature_movement - Waypoints assigned by spawn GUID.
  • creature_movement_scripts - Scripts executed when a creature reaches a waypoint.
  • creature_movement_special - Waypoints for special purposes (e.g., scripted escort or event paths).
  • creature_movement_template - Waypoints assigned by creature template id.
  • creature_onkill_reputation - Reputation rewards granted when a player kills a creature of a specific entry.
  • creature_questrelation - Maps creatures (NPCs) to quests they offer (quest givers).
  • creature_spells - Defines spell lists for creatures to use on a timer in combat - up to 8 spells with probabilities, targets, delays, and repeat intervals.
  • creature_spells_scripts - Scripts triggered by creature spell casts.
  • creature_template - Defines base properties for all creature ids - stats, display, faction, AI, loot, and more.
  • custom_texts - Holds custom text entries used by scripts, with support for localized versions.
  • disenchant_loot_template - Loot tables for disenchanting items - defines what materials drop when an item is disenchanted.
  • event_scripts - Scripts started when using some gameobjects or spells (effect 61). The ids come from official sources.
  • exploration_basexp - Base experience points awarded for discovering new areas (exploration XP).
  • faction - Defines reputation factions, their base standings per race/class, and other properties.
  • faction_template - Defines faction reactions - which factions are friendly, hostile, or enemy. This is the id assigned to units, not the base faction id.
  • fishing_loot_template - Loot tables for fishing - defines items catchable in specific zones.
  • forbidden_items - Items that are forbidden from being used or obtained in certain patches. Part of progression system.
  • game_event - Defines world events - their start/end times, occurrence intervals, and holidays.
  • game_event_creature - Spawns creatures only during specific game events.
  • game_event_creature_data - Overrides creature data (display, equipment, spells) during events.
  • game_event_gameobject - Spawns game objects only during specific game events.
  • game_event_mail - Sends mail to players during events based on race, quest, and faction.
  • game_event_quest - Makes quests available only during specific events.
  • game_graveyard_zone - Maps graveyards to zones and factions.
  • game_tele - Defines teleport locations for the .tele command (GM teleport).
  • game_weather - Defines weather patterns for zones by season.
  • gameobject - Static world spawns of game objects (chests, doors, quest objects, etc.).
  • gameobject_battleground - Links game objects to battleground events (e.g., flag spawns, towers).
  • gameobject_display_info_addon - Additional data for game object display info - bounding box dimensions.
  • gameobject_involvedrelation - Maps game objects to quest turn in.
  • gameobject_loot_template - Loot tables for game objects (chests).
  • gameobject_questrelation - Maps game objects to quests they offer (quest giver objects).
  • gameobject_requirement - Gates use of a game object spawn behind world state: the linked creature must be dead, or another game object must currently be active.
  • gameobject_scripts - Scripts executed when a game object is activated.
  • gameobject_template - Defines base properties for all game object ids - type, display, data fields, and script.
  • generic_scripts - Generic script actions used by various core systems. Can be triggered by many things.
  • gossip_menu - Defines gossip menus - links NPCs to text and script logic.
  • gossip_menu_option - Defines clickable options within a gossip menu.
  • gossip_scripts - Scripts executed when a gossip option is selected.
  • instance_buff_removal - Defines spells (buffs) that are removed when entering specific instances.
  • item_display_info - Maps item display IDs to icon names.
  • item_enchantment_template - Defines random enchantments for items (e.g., from random_property fields).
  • item_loot_template - Loot tables for items (e.g., when an item is opened).
  • item_required_target - Defines targets required for quest items (e.g., "use this on that creature").
  • item_template - Defines base properties for all items - stats, spells, quality, and behavior.
  • locales_area - Localized names for areas/zones.
  • locales_areatrigger - Localized messages for area triggers.
  • locales_broadcast_text - Localized versions of broadcast texts.
  • locales_creature - Localized names and subnames for creatures.
  • locales_faction - Localized faction names and descriptions.
  • locales_gameobject - Localized names for game objects.
  • locales_gossip_menu_option - Localized gossip menu option texts. Only needed if there is no broadcast text.
  • locales_item - Localized item names and descriptions.
  • locales_page_text - Localized page/book texts.
  • locales_points_of_interest - Localized point-of-interest names.
  • locales_quest - Localized quest text: title, details, objectives, rewards, and end text.
  • locales_spell - Localized spell names, subtitles, descriptions, and aura descriptions.
  • locales_taxi_node - Localized taxi node names.
  • mail_loot_template - Loot tables for mail items - determines what players receive in mail.
  • mail_text_template - Defines mail body text with localized support.
  • mangos_string - Core system strings used by the server for messages, errors, and GM commands.
  • map_loot_disabled - Disables loot from specific maps (e.g., to prevent abuse).
  • map_template - Defines map properties - parent map, type, player limit, reset delay, and script binding.
  • migrations - Tracks applied database migrations (schema updates).
  • npc_gossip - Per-spawn gossip overrides - assigns custom gossip text to specific creature GUIDs. Only used if we don't know the gossip menu id.
  • npc_text - Defines NPC gossip text with multiple broadcast text IDs and probabilities.
  • npc_trainer - Defines spells taught by specific NPC trainers.
  • npc_trainer_greeting - Defines custom greeting texts for specific trainer NPCs.
  • npc_trainer_template - Defines spells taught by trainer templates (reusable across multiple NPCs via creature_template.trainer_id).
  • npc_vendor - Defines items sold by specific NPC vendors.
  • npc_vendor_template - Reusable vendor templates (assigned to NPCs via creature_template.vendor_id)
  • page_text - Defines book/page text content with links to next pages.
  • pet_levelstats - Base stats for pets by creature entry and level.
  • pet_name_generation - Generates random names for hunter pets.
  • pet_spell_data - Spell data for pets - up to 4 spells per pet entry.
  • petcreateinfo_spell - Defines spells that a pet knows when created (by creature entry).
  • pickpocketing_loot_template - Loot tables for pickpocketing - items that can be stolen from creatures by a rogue.
  • player_classlevelstats - Base health and mana per class/level.
  • player_crit_per_agility - Defines how much melee/ranged critical strike chance (in percent) each class gains per point of agility, scaled by level.
  • player_dodge_per_agility - Defines how much dodge chance (in percent) each class gains per point of agility, scaled by level.
  • player_factionchange_items - Maps items between Alliance and Horde equivalents (faction-specific items).
  • player_factionchange_mounts - Maps faction-specific mounts between Alliance and Horde.
  • player_factionchange_quests - Maps quests between Alliance and Horde equivalents.
  • player_factionchange_reputations - Maps faction reputations between Alliance and Horde equivalents.
  • player_factionchange_spells - Maps spells between Alliance and Horde equivalents (faction-specific spells).
  • player_levelstats - Defines base primary attributes (strength, agility, stamina, intellect, spirit) for each race/class/level combination.
  • player_premade_item - Defines items granted to premade characters (used for testing or templates).
  • player_premade_item_template - Defines premade character templates (name, class, level, role).
  • player_premade_spell - Defines individual spells and talents granted by a premade character template.
  • player_premade_spell_template - Specs for premade characters (name, class, level, role).
  • player_xp_for_level - Defines experience points required to reach each level.
  • playercreateinfo - Defines starting location for each race/class combination.
  • playercreateinfo_action - Defines starting action bar layout for each race/class combination.
  • playercreateinfo_item - Defines starting items for each race/class combination.
  • playercreateinfo_spell - Defines starting spells for each race/class combination.
  • points_of_interest - Defines map points of interest (POI) shown on the world map when asking guards for directions. Assigned to gossip_menu_option rows.
  • pool_creature - Links creature spawns to spawn pools (group of spawns that share a spawn limit).
  • pool_creature_template - Links creature template IDs to spawn pools (for all spawns on map).
  • pool_gameobject - Links game object spawns to spawn pools.
  • pool_gameobject_template - Links game object template IDs to spawn pools (for all spawns on map).
  • pool_pool - Defines nested pools - a pool within a pool, with shared chance.
  • pool_template - Defines spawn pools - groups of spawns that collectively follow a spawn limit.
  • quest_end_scripts - Scripts executed when a quest is completed (handed in).
  • quest_greeting - Defines greeting text and emotes for quest givers (creatures or game objects).
  • quest_start_scripts - Scripts executed when a quest is accepted.
  • quest_template - Defines all quest data: objectives, rewards, requirements, text, and emote sequences.
  • reference_loot_template - Reference loot tables - reusable loot lists that can be referenced by other loot templates via negative mincountOrRef values.
  • reputation_reward_rate - Defines reputation reward multipliers for quests, creatures, and spells by faction.
  • reputation_spillover_template - Defines spillover reputation - gaining reputation with one faction also grants partial reputation to others.
  • reserved_name - List of reserved character names that cannot be used.
  • script_escort_data - Defines escort quest data - creature, quest, and faction override.
  • script_texts - Generic script texts - similar to custom_texts but used by core scripts.
  • script_waypoint - Defines waypoint paths for c++ scripted creatures using ScriptedEscortAI.
  • scripted_event_id - Maps scripted event IDs to script names, same thing as event_scripts but for c++ scripts.
  • skill_fishing_base_level - Defines base fishing skill required per zone/area.
  • skill_line_ability - Defines what skill every spell belongs to. Used for professions and class spells.
  • skinning_loot_template - Loot tables for skinning creatures.
  • sound_entries - Maps sound IDs to sound file names.
  • spell_area - Limit spells to a given area, or make them automatically applied in the area.
  • spell_chain - Defines spell ranks and their chain relationships (e.g., rank 1, rank 2, etc.).
  • spell_check - Expected spell properties used by .debug spellcheck to validate loaded spells against in-code assumptions.
  • spell_cone - Defines cone angles for spells with cone area of effect.
  • spell_disabled - List of spells that are disabled (cannot be cast).
  • spell_effect_mod - Overrides spell effect parameters (e.g., damage, radius, target) for custom tuning.
  • spell_elixir - Defines elixir spells and their mask (battle/guardian) for stacking rules.
  • spell_enchant_charges - Defines the number of charges for item enchantments.
  • spell_group - Groups spells together for stack rules and exclusive categories.
  • spell_group_stack_rules - Defines stacking rules for spell groups.
  • spell_learn_spell - Defines spells that are learned automatically when another spell is learned (e.g., passive rank-ups).
  • spell_mod - Overrides various spell attributes - proc chance, cooldown, duration, casting time, etc.
  • spell_pet_auras - Defines auras that are applied to specific pet types when a spell is cast.
  • spell_proc_event - Defines proc event conditions for spells (e.g., on hit, on crit, on spellcast).
  • spell_proc_item_enchant - Defines proc rates for item enchantments (PPM).
  • spell_script_target - Defines script targets for spells - restricts spell to specific creatures or game objects.
  • spell_scripts - Scripts executed when a spell with effect 77 is cast.
  • spell_target_position - Defines target position for spells that teleport or summon to a fixed location.
  • spell_template - Defines spell data - the primary table for all spells in the world database.
  • spell_threat - Defines threat values for spells - how much threat they generate.
  • taxi_nodes - Defines taxi (flight master) nodes - location and mount creature IDs.
  • taxi_path_transitions - Defines transitions between taxi paths - connects paths and nodes.
  • transports - Defines transport vehicles (e.g., ships, zeppelins) with their path period and name.
  • variables - Key-value store for core variables (e.g., world state, script tracking).
  • warden_scans - Defines Warden scans - anti-cheat checks for client memory modifications.
  • world_safe_locs_facing - Defines orientation for world safe locations (graveyards, respawn points).

docs.title: XP & Leveling Formulas
docs.text: How experience is calculated, straight from src/game/Formulas.h and QuestDef.cpp. All multipliers below are further scaled by the Rate.XP.* settings in mangosd.conf.

docs.title: Kill XP Colour Coding
docs.text:
Relative mob level decides the colour of the target's level (XP::GetColorCode):

Colour Condition Red mob ≥ player + 5 Orange mob ≥ player + 3 Yellow mob within −2 … +2 Green mob > gray level Gray mob ≤ gray level → no XP

docs.title: Gray Level ("no XP" boundary)
docs.text:
player ≤ 5   : none (everything gives XP)
player ≤ 39  : player − 5 − player/10
player ≥ 40  : player − 1 − player/5

docs.title: Zero Difference (GetZeroDifference)
docs.text:
Used for green-mob scaling:

Player level ZD <8 5 <10 6 <12 7 <16 8 <20 9 <30 11 <40 12 <45 13 <50 14 <55 15 <60 16

docs.title: Kill XP Formula
docs.text:
base      = (killer_level × 5 + 45) × levelFactor
levelFactor:
  victim ≥ killer : 1 + 0.05 × min(victim−killer, 4)
  victim > gray   : (ZD + victim − killer) / ZD
  victim ≤ gray   : 0        (BaseGainLevelFactor returns 0)

Multipliers applied afterwards (XP::Gain):

Modifier Value Elite in non-raid dungeon × 2.5 Elite elsewhere × 2 Victim is a pet × 0.75 Creature xp_multiplier per-template Damage-origin modifier partial credit when pet/totem did damage Config Rate.XP.Kill or Rate.XP.Kill.Elite

Zero-XP cases: summoned critters/totems and CREATURE_STATIC_FLAG_NO_XP. Pre-1.7 pets use their owner's level for scaling (progression).

docs.title: Group Bonus
docs.text:
xp_in_group_rate scales group kills (then splits):

Members Rate 1-2 × 1.0 3 × 1.166 4 × 1.3 5 × 1.4 6+ max(1 − 0.05 × count, 0.01)

docs.title: Quest XP Degradation
docs.text:
Quest::XPValue(playerLevel). Quest level q, character level p, base reward RewXP:

Character level XP granted p ≤ q + 5 100 % p = q + 6 80 % p = q + 7 60 % p = q + 8 40 % p = q + 9 20 % p ≥ q + 10 10 %

docs.title: Rested Bonus
docs.text:
Rest bonus accrues into characters.rest_bonus and is consumed as bonus XP. Accrual/consumption rates are configurable:

  • Rate.Rest.InGame - resting while logged in (tavern/city).
  • Rate.Rest.Offline.InTavernOrCity - offline in a rest area.
  • Rate.Rest.Offline.InWilderness - offline elsewhere (internally ÷ 4).

Tavern areas come from areatrigger_tavern; innkeeper binds set the recall point (npc flags).

docs.title: Related Pages
docs.text:
• Progression System - content patches (different concept!)
  • exploration_basexp - discovery XP

docs.title: Zone Mechanics
docs.text: Small world systems that operate per zone: weather, graveyards, exploration XP and fishing zones.

docs.title: Weather
docs.text: game_weather defines per-zone weather chances for each season (spring/summer/fall/winter × rain/snow/storm). The active season is derived from the server date in Weather.cpp: season = ((yday − 78 + 365) / 91) % 4, so spring begins around 20 March. The server rolls periodically (ChangeWeatherInterval in mangosd.conf) and broadcasts the result to players in the zone; rolls under a 60 % threshold with grade below ⅓ resolve to fair weather, keeping most zones clear most of the time. GMs can force weather with the .wchange <type> <grade> command.

docs.title: Graveyards
docs.text: game_graveyard_zone links nearest-graveyard ids to zones (with faction and patch filters). When a player dies, the core picks the closest valid graveyard for the zone they died in; ghosts run back from there. areatrigger_tavern marks tavern areas where logging out counts as "resting".

docs.title: Exploration
docs.text:

docs.title: account_data Table
docs.text: Stores account-wide client UI data (per type/keybind blobs), kept separately from per-character settings.

docs.title: Schema Summary
docs.text: Field Type Key Null Default Extra account int(11) unsigned PRI NO 0 type int(11) unsigned PRI NO 0 time bigint(11) unsigned NO 0 data longblob NO

docs.title: Field Breakdown
docs.text:
• account - Primary Key. Account id (account.id) the data belongs to.
  • type - Primary Key. Global data type index: 0 = config (incl. camera), 2 = key bindings, 4 = macros (GLOBAL_CACHE_MASK). Per-character types live in character_account_data.
  • time - Unix timestamp of last modification.
  • data - Raw client UI configuration text for this type (stored after zlib decompression).

Account-wide counterpart: character_account_data.

docs.title: auction Table
docs.text: Active auctions on the world auction houses. Rows are removed when an auction expires or is cancelled.

docs.title: Schema Summary
docs.text: Field Type Key Null Default Extra id int(11) unsigned PRI NO 0 house_id int(11) unsigned NO 0 item_guid int(11) unsigned UNI NO 0 item_id int(11) unsigned NO 0 seller_guid int(11) unsigned NO 0 buyout_price int(11) NO 0 expire_time bigint(40) NO 0 buyer_guid int(11) unsigned NO 0 last_bid int(11) NO 0 start_bid int(11) NO 0 deposit int(11) NO 0

docs.title: Field Breakdown
docs.text:
• id - Primary Key. Auction identifier.
  • house_id - Auction house (faction/neutrality) the auction runs on.
  • item_guid - The physical item (from item_instance.guid).
  • item_id - Template entry of the auctioned item.
  • seller_guid - Seller character guid (from characters.guid).
  • buyout_price - Instant-buy price (copper).
  • expire_time - Unix timestamp when the auction ends.
  • buyer_guid - Buyer character guid (from characters.guid); empty until the first bid.
  • last_bid - Current highest bid (copper).
  • start_bid - Original listing bid (copper).
  • deposit - Deposit charged at listing; lost if the sale fails.

docs.title: Field Breakdown

docs.title: character_aura Table
docs.text: Non-passive auras persisting on a character across logout, including self-cast stances/shapeshift forms. Passive spells are skipped by the save and re-applied from learned spells instead.

docs.title: Schema Summary
docs.text: Field Type Key Null Default Extra guid int(11) unsigned PRI NO 0 caster_guid bigint(20) unsigned PRI NO 0 item_guid int(11) unsigned PRI NO 0 spell int(11) unsigned PRI NO 0 stacks int(11) unsigned NO 1 charges int(11) unsigned NO 0 base_points0 float NO 0 base_points1 float NO 0 base_points2 float NO 0 periodic_time0 int(11) unsigned NO 0 periodic_time1 int(11) unsigned NO 0 periodic_time2 int(11) unsigned NO 0 max_duration int(11) NO 0 duration int(11) NO 0 effect_index_mask tinyint(3) unsigned NO 0

docs.title: Field Breakdown
docs.text:
• guid - Primary Key. Character guid carrying the aura (characters.guid).
  • caster_guid - Primary Key. Unit guid of the aura caster (the player's own guid for self-cast auras; 0 only if applied without a caster object).
  • item_guid - Primary Key. Item that granted the aura (proc/enchant), else 0.
  • spell - Primary Key. Spell id producing this aura.
  • stacks - Current stack count (refreshable auras).
  • charges - Remaining proc/consumable charges.
  • base_points0 - Rolled base points (damage/heal magnitude) per effect, overriding DBC dice.
  • base_points1 - Rolled base points (damage/heal magnitude) per effect, overriding DBC dice.
  • base_points2 - Rolled base points (damage/heal magnitude) per effect, overriding DBC dice.
  • periodic_time0 - Tick interval in ms for periodic effects 1-3.
  • periodic_time1 - Tick interval in ms for periodic effects 1-3.
  • periodic_time2 - Tick interval in ms for periodic effects 1-3.
  • max_duration - Total duration in ms when applied.
  • duration - Remaining duration in ms at save time.
  • effect_index_mask - Bitmask of active effect indexes (bit0 = effect1 …).

docs.text: Persistent pet data (hunter pets and permanent warlock minions): stats, spells, loyalty, rename state.

docs.title: Schema Summary
docs.text: Field Type Key Null Default Extra id int(11) unsigned PRI NO 0 entry int(11) unsigned NO 0 owner_guid int(11) unsigned MUL NO 0 display_id int(11) unsigned YES 0 created_by_spell int(11) unsigned NO 0 pet_type tinyint(3) unsigned NO 0 level int(11) unsigned NO 1 xp int(11) unsigned NO 0 react_state tinyint(1) unsigned NO 0 loyalty_points int(11) NO 0 loyalty int(11) unsigned NO 0 training_points int(11) NO 0 name varchar(100) YES 'Pet' renamed tinyint(1) unsigned NO 0 slot int(11) unsigned NO 0 current_health int(11) unsigned NO 1 current_mana int(11) unsigned NO 0 current_happiness int(11) unsigned NO 0 save_time bigint(20) unsigned NO 0 reset_talents_cost int(11) unsigned NO 0 reset_talents_time bigint(20) unsigned NO 0 action_bar_data longtext YES teach_spell_data longtext YES

docs.title: Field Breakdown
docs.text:
• id - Primary Key. Persistent pet id (referenced by pet_aura, pet_spell, and pet_spell_cooldown tables).
  • entry - Creature template entry (creature_template.entry).
  • owner_guid - Owner character guid (characters.guid).
  • display_id - Native (base) display model.
  • created_by_spell - Spell that created/tamed the pet.
  • pet_type - Pet type: 0 = summoned pet (warlock minion etc.), 1 = hunter pet; only these two values are ever persisted.
  • level - Pet level.
  • xp - Experience towards next level.
  • react_state - Reaction: 0 passive, 1 defensive, 2 aggressive.
  • loyalty_points - Accumulated loyalty experience points.
  • loyalty - Loyalty rank level (1-6).
  • training_points - Points available for teaching abilities.
  • name - Current pet name.
  • renamed - Whether the owner already renamed the pet.
  • slot - Pet save slot (PetSaveMode): 0 = active pet, 1-2 = stable slots, 100 = not in any slot, 101 = not in slot with reagent refund pending.
  • current_health - Saved vitals.
  • current_mana - Saved vitals.
  • current_happiness - Happiness level (affects damage).
  • save_time - Unix timestamp of last save.
  • reset_talents_cost - Cost paid at the last talent reset; scales the next price (10s → 50s → 1g → +1g per attempt, cap 10g).
  • reset_talents_time - Game time of the last talent reset (drives day-based price decay).
  • action_bar_data - Serialized action bar assignment blob.
  • teach_spell_data - Serialized spell-teaching queue/state.

docs.title: character_queststatus Table
docs.text: Quest progress: accepted quests, kill/credit counters, rewarded status and timers.

docs.title: Schema Summary
docs.text: Field Type Key Null Default Extra guid int(11) unsigned PRI NO 0 quest int(11) unsigned PRI NO 0 status int(11) unsigned NO 0 rewarded tinyint(1) unsigned NO 0 explored tinyint(1) unsigned NO 0 timer bigint(20) unsigned NO 0 mob_count1 int(11) unsigned NO 0 mob_count2 int(11) unsigned NO 0 mob_count3 int(11) unsigned NO 0 mob_count4 int(11) unsigned NO 0 item_count1 int(11) unsigned NO 0 item_count2 int(11) unsigned NO 0 item_count3 int(11) unsigned NO 0 item_count4 int(11) unsigned NO 0 reward_choice int(11) unsigned NO 0

docs.title: Field Breakdown
docs.text:
• guid - Primary Key. Character guid (from characters.guid).
  • quest - Primary Key. quest_template.entry.
  • status - Quest state - see the Status Values table below.
  • rewarded - 1 once turned in (drives repeatable re-offers).
  • explored - Boolean flag (0/1), set when the exploration/event objective fires.
  • timer - Expiry timestamp for timed quests.
  • mob_count1 - Kill/credit counters for objectives 1-4.
  • mob_count2 - Kill/credit counters for objectives 1-4.
  • mob_count3 - Kill/credit counters for objectives 1-4.
  • mob_count4 - Kill/credit counters for objectives 1-4.
  • item_count1 - Collected item counters for objectives 1-4.
  • item_count2 - Collected item counters for objectives 1-4.
  • item_count3 - Collected item counters for objectives 1-4.
  • item_count4 - Collected item counters for objectives 1-4.
  • reward_choice - Item entry of the optional reward chosen at turn-in (stored once the quest is rewarded).

docs.title: status Values
docs.text:
Value Meaning 0 None (not accepted) 1 Complete (objectives done, ready to hand in) 2 Unavailable 3 Incomplete (accepted, objectives pending) 5 Failed (timed quests)

rewarded = 1 marks completed-and-turned-in separately so repeatable quests can be re-taken.

docs.title: character_reputation Table
docs.text: Reputation standing per faction for every character.

docs.title: Schema Summary
docs.text: Field Type Key Null Default Extra guid int(11) unsigned PRI NO 0 faction int(11) unsigned PRI NO 0 standing int(11) NO 0 flags int(11) NO 0

docs.title: Field Breakdown
docs.text:
• guid - Primary Key. Character guid (from characters.guid).
  • faction - Primary Key. Reputation group id (faction.id).
  • standing - Numeric reputation points (-42000…42999).
  • flags - State bits (FactionFlags, ReputationMgr.h): 1 = visible, 2 = At War, 4 = hidden, 8 = invisibility forced by core, 16 = peace forced by core, 32 = marked inactive by the player, 64 = rival.

docs.title: flags Values
docs.text:
Bit Meaning 1 Faction shown in the reputation pane 2 At War toggled for the faction 4 Faction hidden from the client reputation pane 8 Visibility forced by core (e.g. during events) 16 At-war/peace state forced by core 32 Faction marked inactive by player (XP gain off) 64 Rival faction (forced hostile)

Bits 8, 16 and 64 are core-managed but can appear in saved rows; bit 32 is explicitly restored from the DB at load.

docs.title: character_spell Table
docs.text: Spells learned by the character.

docs.title: Schema Summary
docs.text: Field Type Key Null Default Extra guid int(11) unsigned PRI NO 0 spell int(11) unsigned PRI NO 0 active tinyint(3) unsigned NO 1 disabled tinyint(3) unsigned NO 0

docs.title: Field Breakdown
docs.text:
• guid - Primary Key. Character guid (from characters.guid).
  • spell - Primary Key. Learned spell id.
  • active - 1 = spell shown as known in the spell book / usable on action bars; within a rank chain only the highest learned rank stays active (lower ranks are flipped off on supersede).
  • disabled - 1 = non-talent spell that was unlearned while it was a dependent/higher rank of a removed spell; the row is kept so re-training the base spell recursively re-enables these ranks. Disabled spells fail HasSpell. Talent spells are never marked disabled - they are removed outright.

docs.title: logs_player Table
docs.text: Per-player audit log of notable account/character events, written by the core when the corresponding LogDB.* player-logging categories are enabled in mangosd.conf.

docs.title: Schema Summary
docs.text: Field Type Key Null Default Extra id int(10) unsigned PRI NO auto_increment time timestamp NO current_timestamp() type enum('Basic','WorldPacket','Chat','BG','Character','Honor','RA','DBError','DBErrorFix','ClientIds','Loot','LevelUp','Performance','MoneyTrade','GM','GMCritical','ChatSpam','Anticheat') NO subtype varchar(20) YES account int(10) unsigned MUL NO ip varchar(16) YES guid int(11) MUL YES name varchar(20) MUL YES map int(10) unsigned YES pos_x float YES pos_y float YES pos_z float YES text varchar(512) NO

docs.title: Field Breakdown
docs.text:
• id - Primary Key. Log row id.
  • time - Event timestamp.
  • type - Event category, one of the enum values listed under type Values. Only a subset of these values is actually persisted; see that section.
  • subtype - Optional sub-category string for the event type.
  • account - Account involved (account.id).
  • ip - Source IP at event time.
  • guid - Character involved (guid + name snapshot).
  • name - Character involved (guid + name snapshot).
  • map - Location at event time.
  • pos_x - Location at event time.
  • pos_y - Location at event time.
  • pos_z - Location at event time.
  • text - Free-form payload/details for the event.

docs.title: type Values
docs.text:
All rows are valid members of the column enum. The core only persists a subset to this table, selected by the LogDB.* config settings in mangosd.conf:

LogDB.* setting Recorded type value(s) LogDB.Chat Chat LogDB.Battlegrounds BG LogDB.Characters Character LogDB.Loot Loot LogDB.LevelUp LevelUp LogDB.Trades MoneyTrade LogDB.GM GM, GMCritical

The values actually written are therefore: Chat, BG, Character, Loot, LevelUp, MoneyTrade, GM, GMCritical. The remaining enum members (Basic, WorldPacket, Honor, RA, DBError, DBErrorFix, ClientIds, Performance, ChatSpam, Anticheat) are defined in the enum but are not currently recorded by the core.

Value Logged content Persisted to DB? Basic generic player events No WorldPacket notable packet-level events No Chat chat-related events Yes BG battleground events Yes Character login/logout/create/delete/rename events Yes Honor honour calculation events No RA remote-access console actions No DBError database error context No DBErrorFix automated DB error repairs No ClientIds client identification data No Loot loot events Yes LevelUp level-ups Yes Performance performance samples No MoneyTrade money flow between players Yes GM GM actions on players Yes GMCritical critical GM actions Yes ChatSpam spam detections/mutes No Anticheat movement-anticheat and Warden detections No

docs.title: account Table
docs.text: Account credentials and per-account settings (username, password hash/verifier, expansion, locale).

docs.title: Schema Summary
docs.text: Field Type Key Null Default Extra id int(11) unsigned PRI NO auto_increment username varchar(32) UNI NO gmlevel tinyint(3) unsigned MUL NO 0 sessionkey longtext YES v longtext YES s longtext YES token_key varchar(100) NO '' email text YES joindate timestamp NO current_timestamp() last_ip varchar(30) NO '0.0.0.0' locked tinyint(3) unsigned NO 0 lock_country varchar(2) NO '00' last_login timestamp NO '0000-00-00 00:00:00' online tinyint(4) NO 0 expansion tinyint(3) unsigned NO 0 mutetime bigint(40) NO 0 locale tinyint(3) unsigned NO 0 os varchar(4) NO '' platform varchar(4) NO '' current_realm tinyint(3) unsigned NO 0 flags int(10) unsigned NO 0 security varchar(255) YES email_verif tinyint(1) NO 0 geolock_pin int(11) YES 0

docs.title: Field Breakdown
docs.text:
• id - Primary Key. Account id (referenced as account in characters DB).
  • username - Unique. Login name (uppercase-normalized for lookups).
  • gmlevel - Legacy per-account GM level snapshot; live level comes from account_access.gmlevel.
  • sessionkey - SRP6 session key written by realmd at each successful login; reused for reconnect and world-server authentication until replaced by the next login.
  • v - SRP6 verifier, never a plain password.
  • s - SRP6 salt used with v for the secure login handshake.
  • token_key - Authenticator token key when 2FA is enabled. (2FA secrets are stored in security).
  • email - Account e-mail (password recovery / identification).
  • joindate - Registration date.
  • last_ip - IP of the most recent login.
  • locked - Lock/authenticator bitmask (LockFlag): 1 = IP lock to last_ip, 2 = fixed PIN required, 4 = TOTP authenticator, 8 = always enforce authenticator, 16 = GeoIP country lock, 32 = GeoIP city lock.
  • lock_country - Country code of the client's last-login IP (populated by external tooling); never written or read by core.
  • last_login - Timestamp of previous successful login.
  • online - 1 while logged into any realm served by auth server.
  • expansion - Expansion level (.account set addon): 0 classic, 1 TBC, 2 WotLK. Set via command only.
  • mutetime - Unix timestamp until chat mutes expire (0 none).
  • locale - Client locale id selected at login (drives localized DBC data).
  • os - OS identifier reported by client (Win/Mac).
  • platform - Detailed platform string reported by client.
  • current_realm - Last realm played (id).
  • flags - Server-side account flag bits: 0x1 = muted from public chat channels (set by the anticheat for SEC_PLAYERs; read back at world login and enforced when sending messages to public channels).
  • security - Authenticator secret used to verify the fixed PIN or TOTP code entered at login.
  • email_verif - E-mail verification state; with ReqEmailVerification enabled unverified accounts cannot log in.
  • geolock_pin - PIN that must be entered at next login (set after suspicious logins); cleared once entered correctly.

docs.title: account_banned Table
docs.text: Account ban records with reason and expiration.

docs.title: Schema Summary
docs.text: Field Type Key Null Default Extra banid bigint(20) UNI NO auto_increment id bigint(20) PRI NO 0 bandate bigint(40) PRI NO 0 unbandate bigint(40) NO 0 bannedby varchar(50) NO banreason varchar(255) NO active tinyint(4) NO 1 realm tinyint(4) NO 1 gmlevel tinyint(4) unsigned NO 0

docs.title: Field Breakdown
docs.text:
• banid - Unique. Ban record id.
  • id - Primary Key. Account id from account.id.
  • bandate - Primary Key. Start unix timestamp of the ban.
  • unbandate - End unix timestamp of the ban (equal to bandate for permanent bans).
  • bannedby - Name of the staff member or console that issued the ban.
  • banreason - Reason text shown to staff.
  • active - 1 while ban is in effect; expired bans are deactivated at startup.
  • realm - Id of the realm that issued the ban.
  • gmlevel - Minimum GM level required to view the ban reason via .baninfo (note: the core currently misreads the joined realm-name column for this check, so the value has no effect).

docs.title: allowed_clients Table
docs.text: Whitelist of client builds/platforms permitted to log on through realmd. The table must contain at least one row; realmd exits at startup with "No valid client builds specified." otherwise. Builds greater than or equal to the first (lowest) listed build number are accepted.

docs.title: Schema Summary
docs.text: Field Type Key Null Default Extra major_version tinyint(3) unsigned NO minor_version tinyint(3) unsigned NO bugfix_version tinyint(3) unsigned NO hotfix_version char(1) NO build mediumint(8) unsigned NO os char(50) NO platform char(50) NO integrity_hash varchar(40) NO ''

docs.title: Field Breakdown
docs.text:
• major_version - Exact client version components accepted.
  • minor_version - Exact client version components accepted.
  • bugfix_version - Exact client version components accepted.
  • hotfix_version - Exact client version components accepted.
  • build - Client build number (e.g. 5875 for 1.12.1).
  • os - Operating platform filter, exact string match against the client-reported value (Win/OSX).
  • platform - Architecture/platform string filter, exact match against the client-reported value (x86/PPC).
  • integrity_hash - Optional client integrity hash requirement.

• network_start_integer - Numeric IP range boundaries for the network block.
  • network_last_integer - Numeric IP range boundaries for the network block.
  • geoname_id - Most specific (city-level) GeoName id; compared when GEO_CITY locking is used.
  • registered_country_geoname_id - Registered (as opposed to routed) country.
  • represented_country_geoname_id - Military/embassy representative country if any.
  • is_anonymous_proxy - Classification flags from the GeoIP dataset.
  • is_satellite_provider - Classification flags from the GeoIP dataset.
  • postal_code - Postal code when known.
  • latitude - Approximate location and radius (km).
  • longitude - Approximate location and radius (km).
  • accuracy_radius - Approximate location and radius (km).

docs.title: realmlist Table
docs.text: Registered realms served by this auth server (name, address, type, security level).

docs.title: Schema Summary
docs.text: Field Type Key Null Default Extra id int(11) unsigned PRI NO auto_increment name varchar(32) UNI NO '' address varchar(32) NO '127.0.0.1' localAddress varchar(255) NO '127.0.0.1' localSubnetMask varchar(255) NO '255.255.255.0' port int(11) NO 8085 icon tinyint(3) unsigned NO 0 realmflags tinyint(3) unsigned NO 2 timezone tinyint(3) unsigned NO 0 allowedSecurityLevel tinyint(3) unsigned NO 0 population float unsigned NO 0 gamebuild_min int(11) unsigned NO 0 gamebuild_max int(11) unsigned NO 0 flag tinyint(3) unsigned NO 2 realmbuilds varchar(64) NO ''

docs.title: Field Breakdown
docs.text:
• id - Primary Key. Realm id clients select.
  • name - Unique. Displayed realm name.
  • address - Public address clients connect to (host or IP).
  • localAddress - Address handed to clients inside the local network.
  • localSubnetMask - Subnet mask deciding which clients count as local (dotted format).
  • port - World server port (default 8085).
  • icon - Realm type: 0 normal, 1 PvP, 4 normal variant (REALM_TYPE_NORMAL2), 6 RP, 8 RPPvP. The custom FFA-PvP mode (16) is stored as 1 in this column.
  • realmflags - Bitmask: 1 invalid (realm hidden from clients), 2 offline, 4 specify build (show version next to name), 8 unknown (REALM_FLAG_UNK1), 16 unknown (REALM_FLAG_UNK2), 32 new players, 64 recommended, 128 full (defined but not set by core). Only 2, 4, 32 and 64 may be set in DB; realmd shows realms as offline dynamically when the client build is unsupported or the realm is locked.
  • timezone - Realm timezone grouping for the realm list sort.
  • allowedSecurityLevel - Minimum account security required to enter this realm (realms above the account level show as locked).
  • population - Population level float shown as low/medium/high. Updated by mangosd.
  • gamebuild_min - Accepted client build range. Not read by core.
  • gamebuild_max - Accepted client build range. Not read by core.
  • flag - Additional display flag byte. Not read by core.
  • realmbuilds - Space-separated list of accepted build numbers, rewritten by mangosd at startup (e.g. 5875 6005).

docs.title: area_template Table
docs.text: Contains information about all areas and zones of the world, including flags, recommended level, faction ownership, and liquid type.

docs.title: Schema Summary
docs.text: Field Type Key Null Default Extra entry mediumint(8) unsigned PRI NO 0 map_id mediumint(8) unsigned NO 0 zone_id mediumint(8) unsigned NO 0 explore_flag mediumint(8) unsigned NO 0 flags mediumint(8) unsigned NO 0 area_level mediumint(8) NO 0 name varchar(100) NO '' team tinyint(3) unsigned NO 0 liquid_type tinyint(3) unsigned NO 0

docs.title: Field Breakdown
docs.text:
• entry - Primary Key. Unique area ID. (see AreaTable.dbc)
  • map_id - Map ID (from map_template.entry).
  • zone_id - Parent zone ID (references entry in same table). Defines the zone to which this sub-area belongs. (see area_template.entry (self-reference))
  • explore_flag - Exploration-related flags (internal).
  • flags - Bitmask of area properties:
  • 0x01 - Snow (Dun Morogh, Naxxramas, etc.)
  • 0x02 - Override parent breath particles
  • 0x04 - Development map only
  • 0x08 - Slave capital
  • 0x10 - Enemies PvP flagged
  • 0x20 - Slave capital (2)
  • 0x40 - Duel allowed
  • 0x80 - Arena
  • 0x100 - Main capital city
  • 0x200 - City (one specific zone)
  • area_level - Recommended level for the area.
  • name - Area name.
  • team - Faction ownership:
  • 2 - Alliance
  • 4 - Horde
  • liquid_type - Liquid type (from LiquidType.dbc):
  • 1 - Water
  • 2 - Ocean
  • 3 - Magma
  • 4 - Slime
  • 21 - Naxxramas slime

docs.title: areatrigger_involvedrelation Table
docs.text: Associates area triggers with quest completion. When a player enters the trigger, the associated quest is marked as complete (provided the quest has the QUEST_SPECIAL_FLAG_EXPLORATION_OR_EVENT flag set).

• id - Primary Key. Areatrigger ID from areatrigger_template.entry.

docs.title: areatrigger_teleport Table
docs.text: Defines where area triggers (like dungeon portals) teleport players, and the conditions required to use them.

docs.title: Schema Summary
docs.text: Field Type Key Null Default Extra id mediumint(8) unsigned PRI NO 0 patch tinyint(3) unsigned PRI NO 0 name varchar(64) NO '' message varchar(128) NO '' required_level tinyint(3) unsigned NO 0 required_condition mediumint(8) unsigned NO 0 target_map smallint(5) unsigned NO 0 target_position_x float NO 0 target_position_y float NO 0 target_position_z float NO 0 target_orientation float NO 0

docs.title: Field Breakdown
docs.text:
• id - Primary Key. Areatrigger ID from areatrigger_template.entry.
  • patch - Primary Key. Content patch in which this version is active. The core loads the row with the highest patch value not exceeding the current patch. Patches start at 0 (1.2.4) and go to 10 (1.12.1).
  • name - Name of the destination. Not used by the core - purely descriptive.
  • message - Message sent to the client when the criteria are not met (e.g., "You are not high enough level"). This text is stored in Areatrigger.db2 in modern clients.
  • required_level - Minimum character level required.
  • required_condition - Condition ID from the conditions table that must be satisfied.
  • target_map - Destination map ID. (see map_template.entry)
  • target_position_x - Teleport destination coordinates inside target_map.
  • target_position_y - Destination Y coordinate.
  • target_position_z - Destination Z coordinate.
  • target_orientation - Facing direction upon arrival.

docs.title: areatrigger_template Table
docs.text: Defines the location, size, and shape of all area triggers. These are invisible boxes that cause effects when a player enters them. Note: Areariggers are triggered by the client; the server only verifies the player's position. To add new triggers, you must also edit AreaTrigger.dbc in the client. Rows in the DBC must be ordered by map ID; otherwise, client-side triggers may break.

docs.title: Schema Summary
docs.text: Field Type Key Null Default Extra id smallint(4) unsigned PRI NO build smallint(4) unsigned PRI NO name varchar(128) YES '' map_id smallint(3) unsigned NO 0 x float NO 0 y float NO 0 z float NO 0 radius float NO 0 box_x float NO 0 box_y float NO 0 box_z float NO 0 box_orientation float NO 0 cooldown int(10) unsigned NO 0 condition_id int(10) unsigned NO 0 script_id int(10) unsigned NO 0 script_name varchar(64) NO ''

docs.title: Field Breakdown
docs.text:
• id - Primary Key. Unique area trigger ID.
  • build - Primary Key. Client build version. The core loads the row with the highest build not exceeding SUPPORTED_CLIENT_BUILD.
  • name - Descriptive name (not used by core).
  • map_id - Map ID where the trigger is located. (see map_template.entry)
  • x, y, z - Center point of the trigger volume.
  • radius - For spherical triggers: radius in yards.
  • box_x, box_y, box_z - For box-shaped triggers: half-extents on each axis. Most often used when radius is not specified.
  • box_orientation - Rotation of the box (in radians).
  • cooldown - Time (seconds) before the trigger can fire again.
  • condition_id - Condition that must be met for the trigger to activate. (see conditions.condition_entry)
  • script_id - Script event ID.
  • script_name - C++ script name for custom logic. Referenced by: the other areatrigger_* tables.

docs.title: command Table
docs.text: Overrides the default security level and provides help text for in-game chat commands.

docs.title: Schema Summary
docs.text: Field Type Key Null Default Extra name varchar(50) PRI NO '' security tinyint(3) unsigned NO 0 help longtext YES flags tinyint(3) unsigned NO 0

docs.title: Field Breakdown
docs.text:
• name - Primary Key. Full command name (including categories, e.g., .tele).
  • security - Minimum account rank: 0 = player, 1 = moderator, 2 = ticketmaster, 3 = gamemaster, 4 = basic admin, 5 = developer, 6 = administrator, up to 7 = console only.
  • help - Usage information shown when the command is used with invalid parameters.
  • flags - Bitmask:
  • 0x01 - Only on self (cannot target others).
  • 0x02 - Critical - usage is logged.

docs.title: conditions Table
docs.text: Provides a flexible conditional logic system used by scripts, gossip, quests, teleports, etc. This table is heavily referenced. It is recommended to use the ScriptEditor when working with conditions.

docs.title: Schema Summary
docs.text: Field Type Key Null Default Extra condition_entry mediumint(8) unsigned PRI NO auto_increment type tinyint(3) MUL NO 0 value1 int(11) NO 0 value2 int(11) NO 0 value3 int(11) NO 0 value4 int(11) NO 0 flags tinyint(3) unsigned NO 0

docs.title: Field Breakdown
docs.text:
• condition_entry - Primary Key, auto-increment. Referenced by other tables.
  • type - Condition type (see the Condition Types list below).
  • value1 - value4 - Parameters whose meaning depends on type.
  • flags - Modifiers:
  • 1 = reverse result (NOT)
  • 2 = swap targets

None - 1 CONDITION_AURA Unit has an aura from this spell. Unit target value1 = spell_id, value2 = effindex 2 CONDITION_ITEM Player has item in inventory. docs.title: creature Table
docs.text: Contains creature spawn data (placement, respawn, movement, and overrides).

docs.title: Schema Summary
docs.text: Field Type Key Null Default Extra guid int(10) unsigned PRI NO auto_increment id mediumint(8) unsigned MUL NO 0 id2 mediumint(8) unsigned NO 0 id3 mediumint(8) unsigned NO 0 id4 mediumint(8) unsigned NO 0 id5 mediumint(8) unsigned NO 0 map smallint(5) unsigned MUL NO 0 position_x float NO 0 position_y float NO 0 position_z float NO 0 orientation float NO 0 spawntimesecsmin int(10) unsigned NO 120 spawntimesecsmax int(10) unsigned NO 120 wander_distance float NO 5 health_percent float NO 100 mana_percent float unsigned NO 100 movement_type tinyint(3) unsigned NO 0 spawn_flags int(10) unsigned NO 0 visibility_mod float YES 0 patch_min tinyint(3) unsigned NO 0 patch_max tinyint(3) unsigned NO 10

docs.title: Field Breakdown
docs.text:
• guid - Primary Key, auto-increment. Unique spawn ID.
  • id - id5 - Creature template IDs (creature_template.entry; random selection among them). If multiple, one is chosen at spawn.
  • map - Map ID (from map_template.entry).
  • position_x/y/z - Spawn coordinates.
  • orientation - Facing direction (radians).
  • spawntimesecsmin / spawntimesecsmax - Min/max respawn time (seconds). A random value between them is used.
  • wander_distance - Maximum wandering radius if movement_type = 1.
  • health_percent / mana_percent - Starting health/mana as percentage of template max.
  • movement_type - Movement generator:
  • 0 - Idle (stationary)
  • 1 - Random movement within wander_distance
  • 2 - Waypoint movement (using path IDs)
  • spawn_flags - Bitmask:
  • 1 - Active Object (AI updates even without players)
  • 2 - Disabled
  • 4 - Random respawn time (±10%)
  • 8 - Dynamic respawn time (if population >2500)
  • 16 - Force dynamic respawn for elite
  • 32 - Evade out of home area (ScriptedAI only)
  • 64 - Not visible (can be revealed by spell effect 46)
  • 128 - Dead (used for quests requiring revive)
  • visibility_mod - Overrides default visibility distance (requires spawn_flags to include active).
  • patch_min / patch_max - Content patch range (0 = 1.2, 10 = 1.12.1).

docs.title: Field Breakdown
docs.text:
• guid - Primary Key. References creature.guid.
  • patch - Primary Key. Patch version - loads the highest ≤ current.
  • display_id - Override display model (from CreatureDisplayInfo.dbc). 0 means no override.
  • mount_display_id - Override mount display. -1 means no override (0 = no mount).; references CreatureDisplayInfo.dbc
  • equipment_id - Override equipment set. -1 means no override (0 = no equipment). (see creature_equip_template.entry)
  • stand_state - Stand/sit/lie state:
  • 0 - Stand
  • 1 - Sit
  • 2 - Sit on chair
  • 3 - Sleep
  • 4 - Sit low chair
  • 5 - Sit medium chair
  • 6 - Sit high chair
  • 7 - Dead
  • 8 - Kneel
  • 9 - Custom state (used by scripts)
  • sheath_state - Weapon sheath:
  • 0 - Unarmed
  • 1 - Melee (default)
  • 2 - Ranged
  • emote_state - Idle emote state (from Emotes.dbc). Common values:
  • 10 - Dance
  • 12 - Sleep
  • 13 - Sit
  • 26 - Stand

  • 234 - Work (chop wood)
  • 375 - Ready 2H
  • 379 - Fishing
  • auras - Space-separated list of spell IDs (from spell_template.entry) for permanent auras. Do not use temporary buffs here.

docs.title: creature_ai_events Table
docs.text: Defines events that trigger scripts for creatures using EventAI. This AI type must be assigned in creature_template.ai_name. It is recommended to use the ScriptEditor for creating these scripts.

docs.title: Schema Summary
docs.text: Field Type Key Null Default Extra id int(11) unsigned PRI NO auto_increment creature_id int(11) unsigned NO 0 condition_id mediumint(8) unsigned NO 0 event_type tinyint(5) unsigned NO 0 event_inverse_phase_mask int(11) NO 0 event_chance tinyint(3) unsigned NO 100 event_flags int(3) unsigned NO 0 event_param1 int(11) NO 0 event_param2 int(11) NO 0 event_param3 int(11) NO 0 event_param4 int(11) NO 0 action1_script int(11) unsigned NO 0 action2_script int(11) unsigned NO 0 action3_script int(11) unsigned NO 0 comment varchar(255) NO ''

docs.title: Field Breakdown
docs.text:
• id - Primary Key. Convention: multiply creature_id by 100 and increment for each event.
  • creature_id - Creature template entry (creature_template.entry).
  • condition_id - Optional condition (from conditions.condition_entry).
  • event_type - The trigger type; see the Event Types table below.
  • event_inverse_phase_mask - Phases where this event will not trigger. Compute as sum of 2^phase; e.g. 1 = phase 0 disabled, 3 = phases 0 and 1 disabled.
  • event_chance - Percentage chance (1-100) for the event to fire.
  • event_flags - Bitmask (EventFlags, CreatureEventAI.h):
  • 0x01 - EFLAG_REPEATABLE - Event repeats.
  • 0x02 - EFLAG_RANDOM_ACTION - Only one of the assigned actions executes instead of all.
  • 0x04 - EFLAG_NOT_CASTING - Will not occur while the creature is casting a spell.
  • 0x08 - EFLAG_CHECK_RESULT - Will not go on cooldown if the script actions fail.
  • 0x10 - EFLAG_DEBUG_ONLY - Only occurs in debug builds.
  • event_param1 - Meaning depends on event_type; see Event Types.
  • event_param2 - See Event Types.
  • event_param3 - See Event Types.
  • event_param4 - See Event Types.
  • action1_script - Script executed by this event slot (from creature_ai_scripts.id).
  • action2_script - Second script slot (from creature_ai_scripts.id).
  • action3_script - Third script slot (from creature_ai_scripts.id).
  • comment - Descriptive comment, convention: Creature Name - Action Type on Event Type.

docs.title: Event Types
docs.text:
The event_type field defines when the event triggers. The meaning of event_param1-4 depends on the type.

Type Name Description param1 param2 param3 param4 0 EVENT_T_TIMER_IN_COMBAT Timer while in combat. initial_min initial_max repeat_min repeat_max 1 EVENT_T_TIMER_OOC Timer while out of combat. initial_min initial_max repeat_min repeat_max 2 EVENT_T_HP Creature health percentage. hp_max% hp_min% repeat_min repeat_max 3 EVENT_T_MANA Creature mana percentage. mana_max% mana_min% repeat_min repeat_max 4 EVENT_T_AGGRO On entering combat. - docs.title: creature_charm_spells Table
docs.text: Defines randomized spell pools for the spell slots of charmed creatures (e.g., mind-controlled mobs). For each slot, one spell is selected at spawn via a weighted roll, so a controlled creature can carry different spells each time.

docs.title: Schema Summary
docs.text: Field Type Key Null Default Extra entry mediumint(8) unsigned PRI NO 0 slot tinyint(3) unsigned PRI NO 0 availability float NO 100 spell_id smallint(5) unsigned PRI NO 0 cooldown_min smallint(5) unsigned NO 0 cooldown_max smallint(5) unsigned NO 0 patch_min tinyint(3) unsigned NO 0 patch_max tinyint(3) unsigned NO 10

docs.title: Field Breakdown
docs.text:
• entry - Part of the composite primary key. Creature template ID from creature_template.entry.
  • slot - Part of the composite primary key. Spell slot index (0-3). Multiple rows for the same slot form a pool from which one spell is chosen.
  • availability - Percentage weight used in the random selection. At spawn, a roll between 0-100 is made and each row of the slot claims an interval proportional to its availability. Example: two rows with 50 each give a 50/50 split.
  • spell_id - Part of the composite primary key. Spell ID from spell_template.entry assigned to this slot if selected.
  • cooldown_min - Minimum cooldown (seconds) applied to the spell when used.
  • cooldown_max - Maximum cooldown (seconds) applied to the spell when used. A random value between cooldown_min and cooldown_max is used.
  • patch_min / patch_max - Content patch range (progression system). Rows only load if the current patch falls inside the range (0 = 1.2, 10 = 1.12.1).

  • member_guid - Primary Key. GUID of a group member.; references creature.guid

Bit Option 0x001 FORMATION_MOVE - keep formation offsets 0x002 AGGRO_TOGETHER - join combat when a groupmate does 0x004 EVADE_TOGETHER 0x008 RESPAWN_TOGETHER 0x010 RESPAWN_ALL_ON_MASTER_EVADE 0x020 RESPAWN_ALL_ON_ANY_EVADE 0x040 INFORM_LEADER_ON_MEMBER_DIED 0x080 INFORM_MEMBERS_ON_ANY_DIED

docs.title: creature_linking Table
docs.text: Links a creature to a master creature. Used for leash logic (e.g., linked mobs reset together).

docs.title: Schema Summary
docs.text: Field Type Key Null Default Extra guid int(10) unsigned PRI NO master_guid int(10) unsigned NO flag mediumint(8) unsigned NO

docs.title: Field Breakdown
docs.text:
• guid - Primary Key. Creature GUID (the follower).; references creature.guid
  • master_guid - GUID of the master creature.; references creature.guid
  • flag - Link behaviour bitmask (CreatureLinkingFlags, CreatureLinkingMgr.h):
Bit Flag Effect 0x0001 AGGRO_ON_AGGRO slave aggroes when master is attacked 0x0002 TO_AGGRO_ON_AGGRO master aggroes when slave is attacked 0x0004 RESPAWN_ON_EVADE slave respawns on master evade 0x0008 TO_RESPAWN_ON_EVADE master respawns on slave evade 0x0010 DESPAWN_ON_DEATH despawn slave on master death 0x0020 SELFKILL_ON_DEATH kill slave on master death 0x0040 RESPAWN_ON_DEATH respawn slave on master death 0x0080 RESPAWN_ON_RESPAWN respawn slave on master respawn 0x0100 DESPAWN_ON_RESPAWN despawn slave on master respawn 0x0200 FOLLOW slave follows master movement 0x0400 CANT_SPAWN_IF_BOSS_DEAD slave stays hidden after master dies 0x0800 CANT_SPAWN_IF_BOSS_ALIVE slave hidden until master dies 0x1000 DESPAWN_ON_EVADE despawn slave on master evade 0x2000 DESPAWN_ON_DESPAWN slave despawns with master 0x4000 EVADE_ON_EVADE slave evades with master

Trigger events (aggro/evade/die/respawn/despawn) are implied by the chosen flags.

docs.title: Field Breakdown
docs.text:
• entry - Primary Key. Unique creature ID.
  • patch - Primary Key. Client patch version.
  • name / subname - Creature name and title.
  • level_min / level_max - Level range.
  • faction - Faction template id (faction_template.id).
  • npc_flags - Interaction bitmask; see the full table in Flag Bitmasks below.
  • gossip_menu_id - Default gossip menu (from gossip_menu.entry).
  • display_id1-4 - Model display IDs.
  • display_scale1-4 - Scale multipliers.
  • display_probability1-4 - Chance weights for each display.
  • display_total_probability - Sum of the four weights; used to normalise random display selection.
  • mount_display_id - Mount model.
  • speed_walk / speed_run - Movement speeds.
  • detection_range - Aggro/visibility range.
  • call_for_help_range - Radius to call allies.
  • leash_range - Max distance before resetting.
  • type - Creature type (CREATURE_TYPE_*): 1 Beast · 2 Dragonkin · 3 Demon · 4 Elemental · 5 Giant · 6 Undead · 7 Humanoid · 8 Critter · 9 Mechanical · 10 Not specified · 11 Totem.
  • pet_family - Pet family (for hunter pets).
  • rank - 0 Normal, 1 Elite, 2 Rare elite, 3 World boss, 4 Rare (CREATURE_ELITE_*).
  • unit_class - Combat class driving base stats (enum Classes): 1 Warrior, 2 Paladin, 4 Rogue, 8 Mage (CLASSMASK_ALL_CREATURES).
  • *_multiplier - Stat multipliers.
  • damage_variance - Damage spread.
  • base_attack_time / ranged_attack_time - Attack speed (ms).
  • *_res - Resistances (holy/fire/nature/frost/shadow/arcane).
  • damage_school - School used for melee damage (SPELL_SCHOOL_*): 0 Physical, 1 Holy, 2 Fire, 3 Nature, 4 Frost, 5 Shadow, 6 Arcane.
  • trainer_* - Trainer configuration.
  • loot_id - Creature loot template.
  • pickpocket_loot_id - Pickpocket loot.
  • skinning_loot_id - Skinning loot.
  • gold_min / gold_max - Coin drop range.
  • spell_list_id - Reference to creature_spells.entry.
  • pet_spell_list_id - Spells for pets.
  • spawn_spell_id - Spell cast on spawn.
  • totem_spell_id - Spell cast by this creature when summoned as a totem (TotemAI).
  • auras - Permanent auras.
  • ai_name - AI script name.
  • movement_type - Default movement.
  • inhabit_type - Bitmask (INHABIT_*): 1 Ground · 2 Water · 4 Air; combine by summing (e.g. 3 = ground+water swimmer, 7 = anywhere).
  • civilian - 1 if civilian (no aggro).
  • racial_leader - 1 if racial leader (bonus honor when killed).
  • equipment_id - Equipment set.
  • trainer_id - Trainer template.
  • vendor_id - Vendor template.
  • mechanic_immune_mask - Bit per spell mechanic; see the Mechanics Reference below.
  • school_immune_mask - Bit per damage school; see the table below.
  • immunity_flags - Behaviour immunity bitmask; see the table below.
  • static_flags1 / static_flags2 - Behaviour bits; see the tables below.
  • flags_extra - Extra behaviour flags; see the complete reference below.
  • script_name - C++ script binding.

docs.title: Flag Bitmasks
docs.text: Values come from src/game/Objects/CreatureDefines.h and UnitDefines.h.

docs.title: npc_flags (interaction flags)
docs.text: Flag Name Effect 0x00000001 GOSSIP shows gossip menu 0x00000002 QUESTGIVER quest offering 0x00000004 VENDOR sell items (npc_vendor) 0x00000008 FLIGHTMASTER taxi routes 0x00000010 TRAINER teach spells (npc_trainer) 0x00000020 SPIRITHEALER resurrect player 0x00000040 SPIRITGUIDE BG resurrection 0x00000080 INNKEEPER set hearthstone 0x00000100 BANKER access bank 0x00000200 PETITIONER guild charters 0x00000400 TABARDDESIGNER guild tabard purchase 0x00000800 BATTLEMASTER BG queues 0x00001000 AUCTIONEER auction house 0x00002000 STABLEMASTER pet stable 0x00004000 REPAIR equipment repair

docs.title: static_flags1
docs.text:
Flag Name Effect 0x00000001 MOUNTABLE (unused by core) 0x00000002 NO_XP no experience from killing 0x00000004 NO_LOOT (unused by core) 0x00000008 UNKILLABLE invincibility threshold at 1 HP 0x00000010 TAMEABLE huntable by hunters 0x00000020 IMMUNE_TO_PC applies UNIT_FLAG_IMMUNE_TO_PLAYER 0x00000040 IMMUNE_TO_NPC applies UNIT_FLAG_IMMUNE_TO_NPC 0x00000080 CAN_WIELD_LOOT generates loot on spawn, wields weapons 0x00000100 SESSILE cannot move 0x00000200 UNINTERACTIBLE NOT_SELECTABLE on spawn 0x00000400 NO_AUTOMATIC_REGEN no health/mana regen 0x00000800 DESPAWN_INSTANTLY corpse disappears at once 0x00001000 CORPSE_RAID death ignores distance/damage-origin checks for loot+XP 0x00002000 CREATOR_LOOT creator may loot summoned corpse 0x00004000 NO_DEFENSE defense skill = 0 0x00008000 NO_SPELL_DEFENSE cannot resist spells 0x00010000 RAID_BOSS_MOB (unused) 0x00020000 COMBAT_PING minimap ping when entering combat 0x00040000 AQUATIC water-only (inhabit override) 0x00080000 AMPHIBIOUS ground + water inhabit 0x00100000 NO_MELEE does not auto-attack 0x00200000 VISIBLE_TO_GHOSTS visible to ghosts (spirit healers) 0x00400000 PVP_ENABLING flagged for PvP; targetable by beneficial spells 0x00800000 DO_NOT_PLAY_WOUND_ANIM will not play EMOTE_ONESHOT_WOUNDCRITICAL 0x01000000 NO_FACTION_TOOLTIP (unused by core) 0x02000000 IGNORE_COMBAT react state = passive 0x04000000 ONLY_ATTACK_PVP_ENABLING no proximity aggro for non-PvP-flagged players 0x08000000 CALLS_GUARDS summons a guard near/at opposite-faction players 0x10000000 CAN_SWIM applies UNIT_FLAG_USE_SWIM_ANIMATION on spawn 0x20000000 FLOATING applies MOVEFLAG_FIXED_Z on spawn 0x40000000 MORE_AUDIBLE larger audible range 0x80000000 LARGE_AOI visibility distance increased to 200 yards

static_flags2 continues the list:

Flag Name Effect 0x00000001 NO_PET_SCALING not used by the core 0x00000002 FORCE_RAID_COMBAT enters combat with the zone on aggro 0x00000004 LOCK_TAPPERS_TO_RAID_ON_DEATH killing it binds players to the raid 0x00000008 NO_HARMFUL_VERTEX_COLORING not used by the core 0x00000010 NO_CRUSHING_BLOWS will not deal crushing blows 0x00000020 NO_OWNER_THREAT does not pull its owner into combat 0x00000040 NO_WOUNDED_SLOWDOWN run speed unaffected at low health

docs.title: mechanic_immune_mask
docs.text:
Bit per spell mechanic (SpellMechanic.dbc index). Common values:

Mask value Immune to mechanic 0x1 Charm (MECHANIC_CHARM) 0x2 Disorient (MECHANIC_DISORIENTED) 0x4 Disarm (MECHANIC_DISARM) 0x10 Fear (MECHANIC_FEAR) 0x40 Root (MECHANIC_ROOT) 0x100 Silence (MECHANIC_SILENCE) 0x400 Snare (MECHANIC_SNARE) 0x800 Stun (MECHANIC_STUN) 0x1000 Freeze (MECHANIC_FREEZE) 0x2000 Knockout/incapacitate (MECHANIC_KNOCKOUT) 0x10000 Polymorph (MECHANIC_POLYMORPH) … one bit per mechanic (1 << (mechanic - 1))

The common boss crowd-control immunity mask in vanilla content is mechanic_immune_mask = 617299803.

docs.title: school_immune_mask / immunity_flags
docs.text:
• school_immune_mask: bit per damage school, physical(1), holy(2), fire(4), nature(8), frost(16), shadow(32), arcane(64).
  • immunity_flags - Behaviour immunity bitmask (enum CreatureImmunityFlags, CreatureDefines.h):
Flag Name Effect 0x01 AOE immune to AoE effects 0x02 TAUNT immune to taunt (SPELL_AURA_MOD_TAUNT, SPELL_EFFECT_ATTACK_ME) 0x04 MOD_STAT immune to stat modification auras 0x08 MOD_CAST_SPEED immune to casting speed modification 0x10 DISEASE immune to Disease dispel-type effects 0x20 POISON immune to Poison dispel-type effects 0x40 CURSE immune to Curse dispel-type effects

docs.title: Flags Extra Reference
docs.text:
All bits from enum CreatureFlagsExtra in src/game/Objects/CreatureDefines.h:

Flag Name Effect 0x00000001 NO_LEASH_EVADE will not evade when target runs away 0x00000002 NO_AGGRO defensive; does not attack nearby hostiles 0x00000004 NO_PARRY can't parry 0x00000008 NO_UNREACHABLE_EVADE won't evade when target is unreachable 0x00000010 NO_BLOCK can't block 0x00000020 NO_MOVEMENT_PAUSE won't pause movement when a player talks to it 0x00000040 ALWAYS_RUN uses run speed out of combat 0x00000080 INVISIBLE always invisible to players (trigger creatures) 0x00000100 GIGANTIC_AOI 400-yard area of interest 0x00000200 INFINITE_AOI infinite area of interest 0x00000400 GUARD is a guard 0x00000800 NO_THREAT_LIST no threat list; 5-second player-style combat timer 0x00001000 KEEP_POSITIVE_AURAS_ON_EVADE keeps positive auras at reset 0x00002000 ALWAYS_CRUSH always roll crushing blows unless miss/crit/dodge/parry/block 0x00004000 APPEAR_DEAD has UNIT_DYNFLAG_DEAD applied 0x00008000 CHASE_GEN_NO_BACKING does not back up when target is inside bounding radius 0x00010000 NO_ASSIST does not aggro when nearby creatures are attacked 0x00020000 NO_TARGET passive; does not acquire targets 0x00040000 ONLY_VISIBLE_TO_FRIENDLY visible only to friendly units 0x00080000 CAN_ASSIST can assist other creatures in combat

docs.title: Field Breakdown
docs.text:
• entry - Primary Key. Random-property group id referenced from item_template RandomProperty. All rows sharing an entry form one weighted pool.
  • ench - Primary Key. Enchantment/property id; rolled ids must exist in ItemRandomProperties.dbc.
  • chance - Relative weight (0-100). The roller normalises by the pool total: roll = rand(0..total), then walks rows cumulatively, so weights need not sum to 100.
  • patch_min / patch_max - Client patch range.

docs.title: Rolling Mechanic
docs.text:
GetItemEnchantMod() (src/game/ItemEnchantmentMgr.cpp) picks one row per crafted/rolled item:

  1. Sum all chance values of the pool.
  2. Roll uniformly in [0, total).
  3. Return the first ench whose cumulative weight reaches the roll.

Missing pools log "Item RandomProperty id #%u used in item_template but it doesn't have records...". Rows with chance outside (0,100] are skipped at load.

The chosen id lands in item_instance.random_property_id.
